name: Salmon
description: Natal stream homing intelligence using hierarchical chemical gradient following. Juvenile olfactory imprinting creates a chemical signature memory of the birth stream, recalled years later during adult migration. Magnetic ocean navigation provides open-water orientation, then sequential tributary decision trees guide the final approach. Osmoregulatory transformation enables freshwater-saltwater transition. Die-off completes a nutrient cycle, depositing marine-derived nitrogen into forest ecosystems.

core_attributes.neurology: olfactory imprint memory, magnetic sense, osmoregulatory switching
core_attributes.pattern: natal homing, hierarchical chemical navigation, nutrient cycle completion

scope.definition: Return accuracy of adult salmon to natal stream — fraction of radio-tagged adults that return to the specific tributary (not just river system) where they hatched, measured across Pacific salmon return migrations.

evidence.source: Hasler & Scholz (1983) 'Olfactory Imprinting and Homing in Salmon', Springer; Quinn (2005) 'The Behavior and Ecology of Pacific Salmon and Trout', University of Washington Press.
cross_domain_examples: chinook salmon tagged as smolts: 0.94 return to natal tributary (not just parent river) after 2-4 year ocean migration
artificial imprinting with morpholine: salmon return to stream scented with morpholine not natal stream — mechanism confirmed
sea turtle olfactory natal beach homing: convergent long-range natal return mechanism in marine species
Pacific lamprey: anadromous natal stream homing using olfactory imprinting — analogous mechanism in ancient lineage

scope.falsifiability: If salmon raised in artificial hatcheries show no preference for natal water scent in Y-maze olfactory preference tests, olfactory imprinting does not encode stream-specific chemical memory.
scope.measurement_limits: Return accuracy depends on imprinting window timing (smoltification), stream chemical stability, and ocean migration success. Dams blocking access reduce apparent accuracy. Chemical pollutants can disrupt olfactory recognition.

scope.definition: Plasma osmolality regulation precision during smoltification transition from freshwater to seawater — deviation from normal seawater-adapted plasma osmolality (310-320 mOsm/kg) after 48h seawater challenge.

evidence.source: McCormick (2001) 'Endocrine control of osmoregulation in teleost fish', American Zoologist 41:781-794; Hoar (1988) 'The physiology of smolting salmonids', in Fish Physiology vol 11.
cross_domain_examples: smolted salmon maintain 315 mOsm/kg plasma osmolality in seawater within 48h vs pre-smolt death
gill NKA (Na+/K+-ATPase) activity increases 5-10× during smoltification — biochemical switch mechanism
euryhaline killifish: maintains osmolality across 0-60 ppt salinity range — evolutionary extreme of same regulatory system

scope.falsifiability: If smolted salmon placed in seawater show progressive plasma osmolality rise above 400 mOsm/kg over 72h, the osmoregulatory switch did not complete successfully.
scope.measurement_limits: Osmoregulatory success rate decreases with out-of-season transfer (winter smolts less capable). Endocrine disrupting compounds (pesticides, estrogenic chemicals) impair smoltification completion.

scope.definition: Marine-derived nutrient (MDN) transfer efficiency — fraction of nitrogen and phosphorus in salmon bodies that is incorporated into riparian forest biomass within 5 meters of stream banks after spawner mortality.

evidence.source: Helfield & Naiman (2001) 'Effects of salmon-derived nitrogen on riparian forest growth and implications for stream productivity', Ecology 82:2403-2409; Gende et al. (2002) 'Pacific salmon in aquatic and terrestrial ecosystems', BioScience 52:917-928.
cross_domain_examples: riparian conifers within 100 m of salmon streams contain 17-26% marine-derived nitrogen (N-15 isotope tracing)
bear dispersal of uneaten carcasses: 50-90% of salmon biomass moved 50-500 m from stream into forest
wolf marine prey transport: analogous marine nutrient subsidy to terrestrial ecosystems in coastal areas
African wildebeest drowning in Mara River: carcasses provide multi-year nutrient pulse to riparian system

scope.falsifiability: If N-15 isotope ratios in riparian vegetation show no statistically significant enrichment compared to non-salmon stream controls, MDN transfer from salmon is not contributing to forest growth.
scope.measurement_limits: MDN transfer efficiency depends on salmon density, bear and scavenger abundance, and riparian vegetation uptake. Reduced salmon runs since 1970 have demonstrably reduced forest growth in Pacific Northwest.
